feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: How Lula defied the odds to win Brazil's presidency
entry.summary: Against the odds, Lula has staged a stunning political comeback — but winning Brazil's presidency may prove easier than governing a deeply divided nation.

entry.title: Rule changes could hinder personal prescription drug imports
entry.summary: For years, some people have been buying their prescription drugs from pharmacies outside the U.S. But changes are coming to personal import rules that could make that harder to do.

entry.title: Here's why the Tampa Bay Rays made it to the World Series
entry.summary: The World Series moves to Florida for game 3 between the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers. One reason for the Rays' success is their shrewd trades. More than half their roster came from trades.

entry.title: INVASIVE SPECIES ON SCHOOL MENUS
entry.summary: The Chesapeake Bay, home to blue crabs, striped bass, and other popular seafood, has a new apex predator, the blue catfish. It's invasive and ravenous, growing to more than 100 pounds. But officials hope one of the fish's other qualities might keep it in check: it's delicious.

entry.title: Why some Democrats are hoping for midterm help from independent candidates
entry.summary: Independent candidates say now is the time to increase their numbers on Capitol Hill. And in some races, Democrats see them as their best bet to deny Republicans a majority.

entry.title: A flute prodigy comes into her own sound on debut album
entry.summary: ATC dibs. Out 10/23.NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with Elena Pinderhughes, a jazz flutist known for her work with hip-hop and R&B artists, on her debut solo album, i hope you feel it too.

entry.title: AI giant Anthropic files for an IPO that could break records
entry.summary: The AI company, which makes the popular Claude chatbot, has filed for an initial public offering that could be one of the biggest ever.

entry.title: Special ed diaries: Teachers tell NPR about their most joyous, most difficult moments
entry.summary: What makes special education teaching jobs so hard to fill? NPR set out to find some answers by talking to more than a dozen teachers who do this work every day.

entry.title: U.S. influence in Latin America at stake in runoff election in Brazil
entry.summary: A polarizing presidential election runoff in Latin America's largest economy and biggest democracy pits leftist Lula da Silva's legacy against Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the former Brazilian president.

entry.title: An inside look of the massive data center tearing a Wisconsin community apart
entry.summary: In Port Washington, Wisconsin, there's a data center being built that's as big as 500 football fields. Residents aren't sure if it could save their community or destroy it.
